sentences.text: This animal was a relatively small creature measuring around 2.5 meters in length.
It possessed a small, triangular skull that measured 22.2 cm in length and 13 cm in width.
The premaxilla bone at the front of the snout bore a dental rosette containing five tooth sockets.
Teeth located in positions four through six were very large, while the remaining teeth were smaller and more gracile.
The three crests on the skull were likely covered in keratin, making them considerably taller than the bone alone suggests.
Researchers suggest these structures were likely used for communication rather than defense or combat because they were too delicate for those functions.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered by local miners in the Zorba Extension Opal Field near Coober Pedy.
This specific fossil was purchased in 1988 by the chairman of Comrealty, Mr. Sid Londish.
Another opalized specimen, cataloged as SAM P2381, was discovered in the Andamooka opal fields.
The animal was capable of tolerating the cold conditions of its polar habitat.
In 2008, Smith and Dyke reclassified Umoonasaurus as a member of Leptocleididae within Pliosauroidea.
In 2010, Ketchum and Benson placed Umoonasaurus in Leptocleididae, which they classified within Plesiosauroidea.
The sea where it lived was located at approximately 70° South latitude in the polar regions.
The average temperature of the region where Umoonasaurus lived was estimated at 12.2°C.
